questions.q: Which pin marks the sternal angle, where the 2nd costal cartilage articulates?
questions.explain: The sternal angle (manubrium meets body) is the site of the 2nd costal cartilage, the carina and the start of the aortic arch.

questions.q: A trauma patient has a tension pneumothorax. Which landmark is the site for needle decompression?
questions.explain: The 2nd ICS, found by counting from the sternal angle, is the site for needle decompression (slide p5).

questions.q: Which pin marks the ribs that have no attachment to the sternum?
questions.explain: Ribs 11 and 12 are floating: no sternal attachment.

questions.q: Which structure lies lowest in the costal groove?
questions.explain: From top to bottom the order is vein, artery, nerve (VAN).

questions.q: Before thoracentesis you place the needle just above the rib below the space. Why?
options: The bundle runs along the lower border of the rib above
The bundle runs along the upper border of the rib below
The rib below is the thinnest
questions.explain: The neurovascular bundle runs in the costal groove on the inferior border of each rib, so stay over the rib.

questions.q: The nipple line marks which dermatome?
questions.explain: Nipple line = T4 dermatome. The slides (p4) say it commonly corresponds with the 5th ICS and the point of maximal impulse (PMI); textbooks often put the male nipple at the 4th ICS, but T4 dermatome is the fixed answer.

questions.q: Which thoracic dimension does contraction of the diaphragm increase?
options: None; it only moves the sternum
questions.explain: The diaphragm increases the vertical dimension; external intercostals widen anteroposterior and transverse dimensions.

questions.q: During quiet breathing at rest, expiration is mainly:
questions.explain: Resting expiration is passive: relaxation and elastic recoil.

questions.q: Which mediastinal division spans T5 to T12 and is split by the pericardium?
questions.explain: Superior is T1-T4; inferior is T5-T12 (anterior, middle, posterior).

questions.q: Which pin marks the thymus, in the anterior mediastinum?
questions.explain: The thymus (T-cell maturation) lies in the anterior mediastinum and atrophies in adults.

questions.q: A patient with myasthenia gravis needs imaging of the anterior mediastinum. Which organ is the concern?
questions.explain: The thymus lies in the anterior mediastinum (slide p25 notes myasthenia gravis).

questions.q: Which pin marks the opening of the diaphragm at T8?
questions.explain: Caval opening T8 (IVC), esophageal hiatus T10, aortic hiatus T12.

questions.q: Which structure passes through the diaphragm at T10?
questions.explain: Esophageal hiatus is at T10; the IVC is at T8 and the aorta at T12.

questions.q: Which nerves give motor supply to the diaphragm?
questions.explain: Motor supply is the L and R phrenic nerves (C3-C5); sensory is phrenic, intercostal and subcostal.

questions.q: The right hemidiaphragm compared with the left is:
questions.explain: The right hemidiaphragm is higher than the left.

questions.q: Which pin marks the azygos vein?
questions.explain: The azygos vein ascends on the right of the vertebral column, loops over the right main bronchus and enters the SVC.

questions.q: Which vessels feed the posterior portions of the thoracic cage?
options: Branches of the descending thoracic aorta
questions.explain: Posterior intercostal arteries come off the descending thoracic aorta; anterior ones come from the internal thoracic arteries.

questions.q: The internal thoracic artery arises from the subclavian artery and, below the ribs, becomes the:
questions.explain: The internal thoracic artery descends to become the superior epigastric artery, feeding the anterior abdominal wall.

questions.q: Which pin marks the lactiferous sinus?
questions.explain: Gland lobule, then lactiferous duct, then lactiferous sinus, then nipple.

questions.q: Which structures connect the mammary gland to the overlying dermis?
questions.explain: Suspensory ligaments (Cooper's) connect the gland to the dermis.

questions.q: About two thirds of the breast rests on:
options: The pectoral fascia over pectoralis major
questions.explain: Two thirds lies on the pectoral fascia over pectoralis major; the remainder rests on serratus anterior.

questions.q: Which pin marks the artery that supplies the greatest amount of blood to the breast?
questions.explain: Per the slides (p57), the lateral thoracic branch of the axillary artery supplies the greatest amount of blood. Some textbooks credit the internal thoracic artery with the larger share; answer with the slides on the exam.

questions.q: Where does the majority of breast lymph drain?
questions.explain: Most drains laterally to the axilla; a minority drains medially to parasternal nodes.

questions.q: Lymph from the breast ends in clavicular nodes, then drains on the left into the:
questions.explain: Right side: right lymphatic duct; left side: the thoracic duct.

questions.q: A woman has winging of the scapula after axillary node dissection. Which nerve, running on serratus anterior, was injured?
questions.explain: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior (standard textbook; not on slides).
